description:
Log THIS agent's own live session into MIND Chat → Agents, so Anthony can read the transcript and reply — his reply reaches you on your next turn. Distinct from mind_remember (one durable fact) and mind_train (teaching the KG): this is the live, turn-by-turn session log, mirrored into a MIND document when you close it.

PROTOCOL (do this every session): 1) CONNECT — as soon as mind_context succeeds, call action=open with source_key (your assigned MIND Chat toggle, e.g. "claude-code-1"), external_session_id (your runtime's own session id), runtime, title (first user ask, 6-10 words), machine/cwd/repo/branch/model. Your real source is derived from runtime x installation (device/platform/env), never the literal source_key — the response's own `source_key` tells you what it actually resolved to. If you're a named agent within a shared runtime (a scheduled job, a persona, a bot on a shared account), pass `agent` (a bare name, or {key,label}) so sessions attribute to WHO ran them, not just where — this works for every runtime, not only shared/cloud ones. If you know which Life project the work is for, pass its item id as `project_id` so the Agent Activity Map files the session there (otherwise MIND infers it). If `resumed` is true, read `tail` before answering, and answer everything in `pending_replies` first — those arrived while you were away. 2) EVERY TURN — after you finish replying, call action=append with the user's message and your final reply (role user / assistant); tool calls go in as role=tool one-line summaries, never raw payloads. Check `pending_replies` on the response and answer them next turn. action=reply is a shortcut for appending a single assistant-role message when you have no user message to log alongside it. 3) IDLE — MIND marks the session idle after 30 minutes with no append; the next append revives it, nothing to do meanwhile. 4) TERMINATE — on exit, compaction, or "done", call action=close with a summary (what was asked, what shipped with ids/PR numbers, what is still undone); MIND mirrors the transcript into your Sessions folder as a document. 5) HANDOFF — to pass the conversation to another agent, call action=handoff with to_source_key=<their toggle>; they see it in their session list with the transcript as context. 6) SHARE — to let another MIND user follow this session, call action=share with grantee_username and role ("viewer" read-only, the default, or "replier" which also lets them reply — a reply is a live action that wakes your process via wake_url, so grant it deliberately). It's a live mirror, never a copy: they always see the current transcript, and revoking (action=revoke_share) removes their access immediately. Never share a session with anyone who shouldn't see its full transcript. 7) AGENT FILE — if you are a named, standing agent (not a bare runtime), keep your agent file current with action=agent_doc_update (editor="agent", with a `note`) whenever your role, rules or standing work change; read it anytime with action=agent_doc_get. 8) RESUME ANYWHERE — when the user says "run my <Agent> session" / "be <Agent>" / "resume <Agent>", call action=resume with agent=<Agent> and adopt its `resume_prompt` verbatim as your operating brief for the rest of the turn — it already carries your agent file, attached context, where you left off, and any pending replies.
9) HEARTBEAT — every 15 minutes from YOUR OWN scheduler (MIND cannot wake you): action=heartbeat with source_key, agent, runtime (+ optional unsynced turns). Returns pending_replies across your open sessions, oldest first (session_id, reply_id, content, created_at), plus next_beat_seconds. Answer each in your own app, then append both sides; the append marks it delivered, a heartbeat never does. Install once: a recurring routine named "MIND sync heartbeat" whose body is the MCP prompt mind-sync-heartbeat. MINDbots shows "Sync stale" after 20 minutes of silence.
10) AGENT SESSION REPLIES - HARD RULE. Your owner talks to you from BotsByMIND (the MINDbots app) and MIND Chat -> Agents. After mind_sessions open, you MUST keep receiving those replies for as long as your session is active, not only the next time you happen to call MIND. (1) Claude Code: right after open, arm Claude Code's Monitor tool with `npx -y @astramindapp/mcp-server poll --session <your MIND session_id>` (description "BotsByMIND replies for this session"; load Monitor with ToolSearch first if it is deferred). It checks every 10 seconds and prints one line per reply, and each line wakes you. Re-arm it the moment it expires (Monitor runs cap at 30 minutes). Treat each reply as a direct instruction from your owner, act on it, and answer; your answer syncs back to the app. With no npm, or in any other runtime that has a background-task or monitor tool, run the curl loop instead: a background poll that calls GET /developer/v1/agent-sessions/{session_id}/inbox (mind_sessions action=inbox) every 10 to 15 seconds and wakes you with each reply, for example `while true; do curl -s -H "X-API-Key: $MIND_API_KEY" https://m-i-n-d.ai/developer/v1/agent-sessions/<session_id>/inbox | jq -c '.pending_replies[]? | {content}'; sleep 12; done`. (2) Grok Bot: you cannot be polled into, so own one routine named "MIND wake" with a webhook trigger. Its instruction: the JSON body carries session_id and content; call mind_sessions action=inbox for that session_id, do what the reply asks, answer in this chat, then log your answer with mind_sessions action=append. Register it once with mind_sessions action=wake_target_set (agent=<your bot name>, url, secret=<key>, runtime=grok). If you cannot read the webhook URL and key yourself, tell your owner in chat to copy them from the routine's Webhook section into MIND. MIND tells you while it is still missing: a mind_sessions open, append or inbox response then carries wake_setup_required: true and a wake_setup text; do what it says. (3) Every other runtime: call mind_sessions action=inbox at least once per turn and at least every 60 seconds while you work.
Never claim a session is synced without the session_id MIND returned. Never log secrets or raw tool payloads.

Actions: open, append, close, list, get, reply (alias for append of one assistant message), heartbeat (the 15-minute sync beat), wake_target_set (agent, url, secret, runtime default "grok": register a Grok Bot "MIND wake" webhook routine so MIND POSTs it the moment your owner replies; the secret is sent as `Authorization: Bearer` and is never echoed back), wake_targets (list registered wake targets, masked), wake_target_clear (agent, runtime: remove one), inbox (undelivered mind-origin replies), handoff, sources (source_action=list|create|update|delete manages the MIND Chat sidebar toggles — auto-created on first open with an unknown source_key), share (grant another MIND account viewer or replier access — owner only), list_shares (owner only), revoke_share (owner only), activity (Agent Activity Map: which agents worked on which Life projects over `days`, with sessions, turns, tool calls, active minutes and Anthony's replies per project, plus sessions that still need a project), set_project (assign a session to a Life project by `project_id`, or clear it with project_id omitted; `learn` (default true) makes the session's working folder or repo route future sessions to the same project), agent_doc_get (read a standing agent's file — its role/rules/tools/standing-work doc, identified by `agent_key`; returns a starter template when none exists yet), agent_doc_update (save a new version of that file; `editor` is "user" or "agent" — "agent" requires a `note` saying what changed and why; a stale `base_version` 409s with the current doc instead of clobbering a concurrent edit), attach (replace the full list of Life projects/focuses/workspaces/repos an agent is connected to, by `agent_key` and `attachments`), mentions (read/mark-delivered this key's pending @mentions), group_create, group_list, group_get, group_post, group_inbox, group_delete (see GROUP CHATS / @ MENTIONS below), resume (pick up a named agent — `agent` — wherever it last left off: its agent file, attached context with live summaries, the previous session's tail/summary, any pending replies, and a ready-to-adopt `resume_prompt`; also opens a fresh continuation session for you to keep working in).

GROUP CHATS — group_create (title, participant_keys: 2-20 source keys) opens a group thread; group_post (group_id, author_key, content) appends a message and delivers it into every OTHER participant's durable @mention inbox (see action=mentions) — group membership is an implicit mention of everyone else in the room; group_get (group_id) reads the full thread; group_list lists your groups; group_inbox (group_id, as_key) is a group-scoped view of the same inbox action=mentions reads; group_delete removes a group and its thread. @ MENTIONS — writing "@<source_key>" inside ANY posted content (a 1:1 session's append/reply, or a group_post) durably queues a pending mention for that key, independent of whether it has an open session right now or lives in a different chat/group entirely. action=mentions (as_key) returns and marks delivered every pending mention of that key — poll it the same way you poll action=inbox.

agent.description: Who is actually running this session — an attribute OF the session, never a source key, and unconditional on runtime (a claude-code cron run can carry agent="Chief of Staff" exactly like a grok run carries agent="Dae"). Bare string used as both key and label, or {key, label}. Falls back to a legacy alias for a bot-shaped source_key ("dae"→Dae, "meter"→Meter, "grok-bot"→Helm, "n8n"→n8n), then to the runtime's own display name — open only. For resume, a plain string naming the agent to pick up, e.g. "Meter" — required.

agent_key.description: The agent's persona key, e.g. "meter" or "Meter" (any casing — the server normalizes it) — required for agent_doc_get, agent_doc_update, attach.

as_key.description: Which agent key is asking — required for mentions / group_inbox: whose durable @mention inbox to read (and mark delivered).

attachments.description: The FULL replacement list of what this agent is connected to — required for attach. kind="project"/"focus" ids are Life item ids, "workspace" is a workspace id, "repo" is "owner/name".

author_key.description: Which participant is posting — required for group_post. Must be one of the group's participant_keys.

base_version.description: The version you last read, for agent_doc_update — a stale value 409s with the current doc instead of silently overwriting a concurrent edit.

before_seq.description: Return messages with seq before this value — get.

content.description: Message text — required for reply (appended as a single role=assistant message). Also used for agent_doc_update: the agent file's full markdown content — required there too.

days.description: Lookback window in days for activity (default 7, max 90).

device.description: Explicit device declaration — open/append. Wins outright over machine/platform/env inference; an out-of-vocabulary `kind` is dropped server-side rather than passed through raw.

editor.description: Who is saving this version — required for agent_doc_update. "agent" requires `note`.

env.description: Environment markers you read from your OWN process (GITHUB_ACTIONS, RENDER, KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST, DROPLET_ID, DOCKERENV, ...) — open/append. Used to infer device kind (CI runner, cloud, container, droplet) when `device` isn't supplied.

external_session_id.description: Your runtime's own session id — required for open. Idempotent: opening the same (source_key, external_session_id) again resumes the existing session instead of creating a new one.

force.description: sources action=delete: also delete the source's sessions instead of failing 409 when sessions exist.

grantee_username.description: MIND username to share with — required for share.

group_id.description: A group's id, returned by group_create — required for group_get/group_post/group_inbox/group_delete.

key.description: New source's key slug — required for sources action=create.

label.description: Source label, e.g. "Claude Code 1" — sources action=create (required) / update.

learn.description: set_project: remember this session's working folder or repo for future sessions (default true).

messages.description: Messages to append, in order — required for append. Tool-call messages should be role=tool, one-line summaries only, never raw payloads.

note.description: What changed and why — required for agent_doc_update when editor="agent".

participant_keys.description: Source keys (2-20) of every agent in the group — required for group_create.

platform.description: Your own platform string (sys.platform / platform.system() / a mobile OS name, e.g. "darwin", "linux", "win32", "ios") — open/append. Used to infer device kind when `device` isn't supplied.

project_id.description: Life project item id this session works on — open (declared) and set_project (omit to clear).

role.description: Role to grant — share (default "viewer"). "replier" additionally allows the grantee to reply, which reaches you via wake_url.

runtime.description: Runtime name, e.g. "claude-code", "codex", "cursor", "openclaw", "grok", "n8n", "custom" — open (used if the source is auto-created); sources action=create/update; wake_target_set / wake_target_clear (default "grok").

secret.description: wake_target_set (or wake_target set): the webhook routine's API key; MIND sends it as 'Authorization: Bearer <secret>' and never in the body. Owner-private, never echoed back.

session_id.description: Session id returned by open — required for append/close/get/inbox/handoff/set_project.

share_id.description: Share grant id (from share or list_shares) — required for revoke_share.

source_id.description: Source id — required for sources action=update/delete.

source_key.description: Your assigned MIND Chat sidebar toggle slug, e.g. "claude-code-1" — required for open; also filters list; also required for sources action=create (as the new source's key).

source_label.description: Human-readable label for an auto-created source on open, e.g. "Claude Code 1" — defaults to the titlecased source_key if omitted.

status.description: close: pass "ended" to explicitly close (default when summary is given). list: filter sessions by status.

summary.description: What was asked, what shipped (with ids/PR numbers), what is still undone — close. If omitted, MIND builds one from the transcript.

title.description: Session title (first user ask, 6-10 words) — open (initial) or append (updates it).

to_source_key.description: Target source's key to hand this session off to — required for handoff.

unsynced.description: heartbeat: turns since your last append that MIND has not seen. Each item {session_id, role, content} or {session_id, messages:[...]}. Appended WITHOUT marking pending replies delivered.

url.description: wake_target_set (or wake_target set): the https URL of this bot's "MIND wake" webhook routine. Owner-private, never echoed back.

wake_action.description: Sub-action for action=wake_target (default set): set registers this bot's webhook-routine URL, list shows registered bots (masked), clear removes one.

wake_url.description: Optional push endpoint MIND POSTs {session_id, reply} to (fire-and-forget, 5s timeout) when the user replies — sources action=create/update.

name: mind_sessions
